heroText: Mogadishu is Somalia's Indian Ocean capital, a historic Swahili and Arab trading port whose old stone quarters sit beside the wide sands of Lido Beach. First-time visitors should walk the narrow lanes of Hamar Weyne's old town, see the coral-stone ruins of Mogadishu Cathedral, and shop for spices and fabric at Bakara Market. Aden Adde International Airport anchors a secured coastal zone, and travel here requires careful planning given the current security situation.

areas.name: Hamar Weyne
areas.text: Hamar Weyne is Mogadishu's oldest quarter, a maze of coral-stone buildings and narrow lanes near the historic port and fish market.

areas.name: Shangani
areas.text: Shangani is a coastal district near the old Italian quarter, home to the cathedral ruins and some of the city's oldest architecture.

areas.name: Wardhiigley
areas.text: Wardhiigley is a central district housing government offices and some of the city's more secure commercial areas.

areas.name: Airport zone (Aden Adde / Halane)
areas.text: The Aden Adde airport zone is a heavily secured coastal compound housing the airport, embassies and international organisations.

airports.name: Aden Adde International Airport (MGQ)
airports.search: Aden Adde International Airport, Mogadishu, Somalia
airports.text: Aden Adde International Airport sits inside a secured coastal compound, and most visitors arrange transfers and accommodation through the same protected zone.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Aden Adde International Airport (MGQ) and central Mogadishu before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Most visits to Mogadishu are arranged around the secured airport zone, where hotels, embassies and international offices cluster together. Hamar Weyne and Shangani reward a guided daytime visit for their old-town architecture, while Wardhiigley suits official and business trips needing central government access.
hotelIntro: Mogadishu hotel choice is largely dictated by security: most visitors base themselves in the protected airport zone with vetted transport, while day visits to Hamar Weyne or Shangani are typically arranged with local guides and advance planning.
rentalCars: Independent car rental is not advisable; visitors typically arrange vetted drivers and security escorts through their hotel or a local fixer for any movement around the city.

travelTips.title: Security planning
travelTips.text: Arrange any Mogadishu visit well ahead through a trusted local contact, hotel or security provider, and confirm current travel advisories before booking.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Base in the secured airport zone, where most international hotels, embassies and aid offices operate behind controlled access.

travelTips.title: Old town visits
travelTips.text: Visit Hamar Weyne and the cathedral ruins during daylight hours with a local guide rather than independently.

travelTips.title: Cash and connectivity
travelTips.text: Carry US dollars for most transactions, since Somali shillings are used mainly for small everyday purchases.

nearbyIdeas.text: The historic Mogadishu Old Port sits beside Hamar Weyne, still used by traditional fishing dhows much as it has been for centuries.

history.text: Ibn al-Mujawir mentions the Banu Majid, who fled the Mundhiriya region in Yemen in the year 1159 and settled in Mogadishu and also traders from the port towns of Abyan and Haram.

history.label: 15th century
history.text: Vasco da Gama, who passed by Mogadishu in the 15th century, noted that it was a large city with houses of four or five stories high and large palaces in its centre and many mosques with cylindrical minarets.
Duarte Barbosa, the famous Portuguese traveller, wrote about Mogadishu (c 1517–1518):It has a king over it, and is a place of great trade in merchandise.
In 1542, the Portuguese commander João de Sepúvelda led a small fleet on an expedition to the Somali coast.
In World War II it was captured by British forces in February 1941.
After World War II Mogadishu was made the capital of the Trust Territory of Somaliland, an Italian administered fiduciary political entity under the UN mandate, for ten years (1950–1960).
On 1 July 1960, the two territories united to form the Somali Republic, with Mogadishu serving as the nation's capital.
